## What the plan does

Replaces the environment-brittle `assert _ppid(detached_pid) == "1"` at
`tests/test_workflow_setsid_detach_convention.py:124` with a predicate over the
set of pids the kernel may legitimately reparent into —
`{pytest} ∪ ancestors(pytest) ∪ {1}` — plus a separate assert that the target is
not the dead wrapper. Grounded in `find_new_reaper`: an orphan is adopted by the
nearest `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` ancestor of the dying parent, else the
pid-namespace init, so the new parent is always an ancestor of the wrapper and
never inside its session. The old literal is the special case of this predicate
on hosts with no subreaper in the ancestry. This does NOT loosen the case to a
bare liveness check, which the task body explicitly forbids.

The reaper set is derived from pytest rather than the wrapper because
`communicate()` has already reaped the wrapper by assertion time (measured:
`alive_after_communicate=False`), and the wrapper is a direct child of pytest, so
`ancestors(wrapper) == {pytest} ∪ ancestors(pytest)`.

Also adds one committed companion case,
`test_reaper_set_excludes_a_live_child`, pinning that the set rejects a live
descendant — this is what keeps the membership assert from going vacuous.

## Review record — minimum plan-review floor (`wf-fix`)

- `verify_plan.py`: PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 WARN at v4 (see the `epm:plan-verify` marker
  immediately preceding).
- Claude `critic`, Methodology lens: **round 1 REVISE → round 2 APPROVE.**
  - Round 1 found a real defect: v2's negative control (drop `setsid`, expect
    the new block to fail) dies two asserts UPSTREAM at the pg-leader wait loop,
    so `killpg` never fires and the replaced block is never reached — the
    control would have reported FAIL for every implementation, including a
    vacuously-true one. **Confirmed by measurement** before accepting
    (`pgid(detached)=872351` == `wrapper.pid`, `detached=872353`). v3 replaced
    it with the committed discrimination case above.
  - Round 2 APPROVEd with three cosmetic items, all applied in v4: removed a
    phantom "0.2 s settle" the diff never contained, tightened the companion
    docstring to the descendant-superset argument (session membership is
    fork-inherited, so every possible in-session parent is a descendant of
    pytest and the upward walk excludes all of them at any depth), and disclosed
    the future-call-site-drift residual in the blind-spot enumeration.
- **One round-2 answer was refuted by execution and corrected in v4.** The
  critic reasoned that a full-file run under `unshare -Urpf --mount-proc` was a
  sound acceptance gate. Running it: pristine tree → `1 failed, 4 passed in
  10.34s`, failing at **line 119**, because inside the namespace the plain child
  (`sleep`, pgid = wrapper.pid, verified against the full namespace process
  table so not a reused pid) survives both `killpg` and a direct `SIGTERM`,
  while the host reaps it in 0.25 s. The namespace reproduces the ADOPTION leg
  faithfully (target `1`, three independent probes) but not the group-kill leg.
  v4 therefore scopes #2112's third context to an adoption-target scenario probe
  and forbids the full-file run as a gate (new kill criterion 4). The signal
  divergence is recorded as an unexplained namespace-specific observation — not
  root-caused, out of scope for a one-assertion infra task.
